examples.ko: 한옥이 산 아래에 고즈넉이 자리 잡고 있어요.
examples.en: The hanok sits quietly at the foot of the mountain.
The temple stands quietly in the forest.

examples.ko: 눈 내리는 밤, 마을이 고즈넉이 잠들어 있어요.
examples.en: On the snowy night, the village sleeps in peaceful stillness.
We sat quietly and drank tea.

examples.ko: 오래된 집이 골목 끝에 고즈넉이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: An old house remains quietly at the end of the alley.
Under the moonlight, the lake shines serenely.

explain: 풍경이나 분위기를 묘사하는 글에서 주로 보이고, 평소 대화에서는 '조용히'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '고즈넉하게'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 작은 절이 숲속에 고즈넉하게 서 있어요.
phrases.en: A small temple stands quietly in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고즈넉이'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 이 형태도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 고즈넉이, and common in speech too.

phrases.en: The village is sleeping quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소 대화에서는 '고즈넉이' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used instead of 고즈넉이 in daily conversation.

phrases.en: Grandfather is sitting quietly on the porch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차분하고 조용한 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paints a calm and quiet scene.

explain_en: It mostly shows up in writing that describes scenery or mood, while in ordinary conversation people more often say '조용히'. '고즈넉하게' is also used.

t90.ax: We sat quietly and drank tea.

examples.en: The temple in the early morning is quiet and peaceful.
The snow-covered village was truly serene.
I want to read a book in a calm, quiet cafe.

examples.ko: 한옥 마을의 골목이 고즈넉해서 산책하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The alleys of the hanok village are tranquil, so they are nice for walks.
After sunset, the street became even quieter and more peaceful.
I gazed for a long time at the calmly flowing river.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 없다는 뜻이 중심인데, '고즈넉하다'는 호젓하고 차분한 분위기까지 느껴질 때 써요. 절, 한옥, 시골길 같은 풍경에 잘 어울려요. 도서관이 조용할 때는 '조용하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I like the serene atmosphere of this tea house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소의 느낌을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for describing a place's feel.

phrases.en: I rested a day in a quiet village in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 차분한 시골 풍경에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits quiet, peaceful countryside scenes.

phrases.en: The street isn't serene because there are many tourists.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차분한 분위기가 없을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for when the calm feeling is missing.

explain_en: '조용하다' is mainly about the absence of noise, while '고즈넉하다' also carries a secluded, calm mood. It suits scenes like temples, hanok, and country roads. For a quiet library, '조용하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: A deep, gentle fragrance spread through the room.
He gazed at his wife with deep feeling.
It's a night when the moonlight shines softly.
The sound of a bell echoed deeply from the mountain temple.
The rich scent of coffee reached my nose.

examples.ko: 그분은 그윽이 웃으며 제 이야기를 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: She listened to my story with a deep, gentle smile.

explain: 깊고 은은하게 느껴지는 모습이에요. 향기, 눈빛, 달빛, 소리 같은 말과 어울려요. '깊이'는 정도만 말하지만 '그윽이'는 고요하고 은은한 느낌이 더해져요.

phrases.en: The coffee aroma spreads gently and deeply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그윽이'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '그윽이' and more natural in speech.

phrases.en: I like the subtle, deep scent of the tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 향기와 가장 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, most often paired with scents.

phrases.en: He looked at me with a deep, tender gaze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊고 따뜻한 마음이 느껴지는 눈빛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gaze full of deep, warm feeling.

explain_en: It describes something that feels deep and subtle. It goes with words like fragrance, gaze, moonlight and sound. '깊이' only speaks of degree, but '그윽이' adds a quiet, subtle feeling.

t90.ax: He gazed at his wife with deep feeling.

examples.en: If you climb the spiral staircase, you reach the observation deck.
A snail's shell is coiled in a spiral.
The smoke rose, drawing a spiral.
Our galaxy is spiral-shaped.
The parking lot ramp spirals, so it's hard to drive.
I picked up a spiral-shaped shell on the beach.

explain: '나선형 계단'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 많이 써요. '원형'은 한 바퀴 돌아 닫힌 동그라미이고, 나선형은 돌면서 위나 바깥으로 이어지는 모양이에요. 달팽이, 소라, 은하, 계단을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Our house has a spiral staircase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나선형과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with this word.

phrases.en: The smoke rose in a spiral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '으로'를 붙여 움직이는 모양을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 으로, it describes the shape of movement.

phrases.en: A conch shell has a spiral structure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 어떻게 이루어졌는지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for describing how something is built.

explain_en: It is often used to modify a noun that follows, as in '나선형 계단' (spiral staircase). '원형' is a closed circle, while '나선형' keeps winding upward or outward as it turns. It often comes up when talking about snails, conch shells, galaxies and staircases.

examples.en: This writer's descriptive power is really outstanding.

examples.ko: 글쓰기 수업에서 묘사력을 기르는 연습을 많이 해요.
examples.en: In writing class we do a lot of practice to build descriptive skill.
It was a moving poem because it was written with delicate descriptive skill.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 배경 묘사력이 특히 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: That movie's depiction of the setting was especially impressive.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 묘사력이 부족해서 이야기를 짧게만 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling lacks descriptive skill, so they only tell stories briefly.

examples.ko: 묘사력 있는 문장 덕분에 풍경이 눈앞에 그려졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the vivid sentences, I could picture the scenery in front of my eyes.

explain: '표현력'은 말이나 글 전체를 두루 가리키지만, '묘사력'은 모습이나 분위기, 장면을 생생하게 그려 내는 힘에 가까워요. '뛰어나다', '부족하다', '기르다'와 자주 함께 써요. 주로 글쓰기나 소설, 영화 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: That novelist is excellent at describing scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 말로 장면을 잘 그려 낸다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for vividly describing scenes in writing or speech.

phrases.en: I build my descriptive skill by writing a diary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연습해서 표현하는 힘을 키운다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when practicing to improve descriptive ability.

phrases.en: My writing still lacks descriptive power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이 생생하지 않을 때 자신의 약점을 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out a weakness when writing isn't vivid enough.

explain_en: '표현력' covers expressive ability in speech and writing in general, while '묘사력' is closer to the power to paint an appearance, mood or scene vividly. It often goes with '뛰어나다', '부족하다' and '기르다'. You mostly hear it when people talk about writing, novels and films.

examples.en: The cat's eyes flashed in the darkness.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 좋은 생각이 번득여서 메모했어요.
examples.en: A good idea flashed into my mind during the meeting, so I took a note.
I can see the window glass flashing in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 그의 눈에서 번득이던 빛이 잊히지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't forget the glint that flashed in his eyes.
Lightning flashed, and soon thunder rolled.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 가끔 번득이는 아이디어를 내요.
examples.en: That student sometimes comes up with brilliant ideas.

explain: 빛이 잠깐 강하게 빛날 때 쓰고, 좋은 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때도 비유로 써요. '번뜩이다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 눈빛이나 아이디어를 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I saw his eyes flash.
phrases.nuance_ko: '번득이다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with almost the same meaning as 번득이다.

phrases.en: His flashing gaze was scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날카롭고 강한 눈빛을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a sharp, intense gaze.

phrases.en: If you have a bright idea, please tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a good idea that suddenly appears.

explain_en: It is used when light shines strongly for a moment, and figuratively when a good idea suddenly comes to mind. It is used almost the same as '번뜩이다'. It especially appears when describing a look in the eyes or an idea.

examples.ko: 동생은 선물을 받고 하루 종일 벙글벙글했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling beamed all day after getting the present.
The baby beams when it sees its mom.

examples.ko: 무슨 좋은 일이 있어요? 아침부터 벙글벙글하네요.
examples.en: Did something good happen? You've been beaming since this morning.
Dad smiled broadly at the news that I passed.

examples.ko: 벙글벙글하는 얼굴을 보니 저도 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Seeing that beaming face made me feel good too.
My friend was beaming because it was payday, and bought us a meal.

explain: 소리는 내지 않고 입을 크게 벌려 환하게 웃는 모습이에요. '벙글벙글 웃다'처럼 '웃다' 앞에 부사로 붙여서도 말해요. '싱글벙글'도 비슷하게 기분 좋은 웃음을 나타내요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is beaming after passing the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벙글벙글'은 부사로도 쓰여서 '웃다' 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 벙글벙글 also works as an adverb placed before 웃다 (to laugh).

phrases.en: Grandmother beams whenever she sees her grandchild.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 기분이 아주 좋아서 웃는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, showing a smile from being in a great mood.

phrases.en: I opened the gift with a beaming face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 바꿔서 '얼굴'을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Takes -는 to modify 얼굴 (face).

explain_en: It shows someone smiling brightly with a wide mouth but without making a sound. It is also used as an adverb before '웃다', as in '벙글벙글 웃다'. '싱글벙글' expresses a similar happy smile.

t90.ax: The baby beams when it sees its mom.

en: to be inexplicable; to be beyond comprehension; to be wondrous

examples.en: The pyramids are truly mysterious structures.
That incident is still a mystery.
Strange, unexplainable things happened one after another.
There are many puzzling phenomena in nature.

examples.ko: 과학으로 설명할 수 없어서 더 불가사의하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It can't be explained by science, so it feels all the more mysterious.
I read about the seven wonders of the world in a book.

explain: 이해하거나 설명할 수 없을 만큼 이상하고 놀라울 때 써요. '신기하다'는 가벼운 놀라움이고, 불가사의하다는 이유를 알 수 없는 큰 수수께끼 같은 느낌이에요. 글에서 많이 쓰고, '세계 7대 불가사의'처럼 명사 '불가사의'로도 써요.

phrases.example: 오래된 성에서 불가사의한 일이 자주 일어났대요.
phrases.en: I heard that inexplicable things often happened in the old castle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명할 수 없는 이상한 일이나 사건을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing for describing strange events that cannot be explained.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 그걸 어떻게 알았는지 정말 불가사의하네요.
phrases.en: How that person knew it is really beyond understanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-네요'를 붙이면 알게 된 사실에 놀라는 느낌이 나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -네요 gives a feeling of surprise at what you have just noticed.

phrases.example: 그 이야기는 저에게 너무 불가사의하게 느껴졌어요.
phrases.en: That story felt so mysterious and beyond understanding to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 어떤 것이 이해할 수 없게 느껴진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it says that something feels beyond understanding.

explain_en: It is used when something is so strange and amazing that it can't be understood or explained. '신기하다' is light wonder, while 불가사의하다 feels like a big riddle with no known reason. It is common in writing and also works as the noun '불가사의', as in '세계 7대 불가사의'.

en: to be beautiful; to be lovely

examples.en: The bride is truly lovely.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 아가씨가 꽃을 들고 서 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty young lady is standing there holding flowers.

examples.ko: 아이가 웃는 모습이 참 어여뻐 보여요.
examples.en: The child looks so lovely when smiling.
My grandmother calls me her lovely granddaughter.
When spring came, the flowers bloomed beautifully.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 한복을 입은 아이들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The children in pretty hanbok lined up.

explain: '예쁘다'를 좀 더 정감 있고 예스럽게 말하는 느낌이에요. 노랫말이나 시, 어른이 아이를 귀여워하는 말에서 어울려요. 친구끼리 일상 대화에서는 보통 '예쁘다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Lovely flowers have bloomed in the garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예쁜 꽃'보다 정감 있고 예스러운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Warmer and more old-fashioned than '예쁜 꽃'.

phrases.en: You look really lovely in hanbok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 모습이 곱다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how lovely someone looks.

phrases.en: Flowers have bloomed prettily along the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 곱게 핀 모습을 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when describing flowers blooming beautifully.

explain_en: It feels like a warmer, slightly old-fashioned way of saying '예쁘다'. It suits song lyrics, poems, and adults fondly talking about children. In everyday talk between friends, people usually just say '예쁘다'.

examples.ko: 새 직장에서 저만 천덕꾸러기가 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: At my new job I feel like I'm the only one treated as a nuisance.

examples.ko: 동생이 태어난 뒤로 저는 집에서 천덕꾸러기 취급을 받았어요.
examples.en: After my sibling was born, I was treated like a nuisance at home.

examples.ko: 천덕꾸러기로 남은 낡은 소파를 결국 버렸어요.
examples.en: I finally threw out the old sofa that nobody wanted.

examples.ko: 저는 어디에 가도 천덕꾸러기는 아니었으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope I'm never the unwanted one wherever I go.
The game console that was once popular is now a nuisance.

examples.ko: 모두가 천덕꾸러기라고 놀렸지만 그 아이는 꿋꿋했어요.
examples.en: Everyone teased him as a burden, but the child stayed strong.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 쓸모없어져서 푸대접받는 물건에도 써요. '천덕꾸러기 취급을 받다', '천덕꾸러기가 되다'가 자주 쓰는 형태예요. '골칫덩어리'는 문제를 일으켜 곤란한 존재이고, 천덕꾸러기는 사람들에게 푸대접받는 쪽이에요.

phrases.example: 이사 온 뒤로 천덕꾸러기 신세가 되었어요.
phrases.en: Since moving here I've ended up as the unwanted one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 푸대접받는 처지를 말할 때 '신세'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '신세' to describe a situation of being neglected.

phrases.example: 낡은 소파가 이제 집에서 천덕꾸러기가 됐어요.
phrases.en: The old sofa has become a nuisance in the house now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸모없어진 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for things that have lost their use.

phrases.en: At the meeting I felt like the unwanted one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 환영받지 못한다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel unwelcome.

explain_en: It is used for people and also for things that became useless and are treated poorly. Common forms are '천덕꾸러기 취급을 받다' and '천덕꾸러기가 되다'. '골칫덩어리' is someone who causes trouble, while a 천덕꾸러기 is the one who gets treated badly.

t90.ax: I hope I'm never the unwanted one wherever I go.

en: to be turbulent; to be full of ups and downs

examples.en: My grandmother told me about her life full of ups and downs.
That singer's life has really been full of ups and downs.

examples.ko: 파란만장했던 한 해를 보내고 새해를 맞았어요.
examples.en: We saw off a turbulent year and welcomed the new one.

examples.ko: 파란만장하게 살아온 그분의 이야기가 책으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The story of that person, who lived through many ups and downs, came out as a book.

examples.ko: 그의 인생은 파란만장하지만 늘 웃음을 잃지 않아요.
examples.en: His life is full of turmoil, but he never loses his smile.

examples.ko: 파란만장하다는 말은 그분의 삶에 딱 맞아요.
examples.en: The word 'eventful' fits that person's life perfectly.

explain: 행복과 불행이 크게 오르내린 긴 삶이나 이야기에 써요. 주로 '삶, 인생, 일생' 같은 말을 꾸미고, 하루짜리 일에는 어색해요. 일이 많았던 한 해에는 '다사다난하다'도 써요.

phrases.en: A movie was made about his turbulent life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 삶 전체를 말할 때 '일생'과 함께 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 일생 to describe a person's whole life.

phrases.en: My grandfather's youth was full of ups and downs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 어떤 시기가 굴곡이 많았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form, used to say a period of life was full of ups and downs.
phrases.en_equiv: was full of ups and downs

phrases.example: 그 책은 한 여인의 파란만장한 이야기예요.
phrases.en: That book is the turbulent story of one woman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 영화처럼 굴곡 많은 이야기를 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a story with many twists, like a book or movie.

explain_en: It is used for a long life or story with big swings between joy and hardship. It usually modifies words like '삶', '인생' and '일생' and sounds odd for a single day's events. For a busy, eventful year, '다사다난하다' is also used.

t90.ax: We saw off a turbulent year and welcomed the new one.

examples.ko: 그 의사 선생님은 우리 가족의 구원자예요.
examples.en: That doctor is our family's savior.
The friend who showed up then was a lifesaver for me.

examples.ko: 위기에 빠진 팀에 새 감독이 구원자가 되었어요.
examples.en: The new manager became the savior of the team in crisis.
People called him the savior of the village.

examples.ko: 저는 누구의 구원자도 아니고 그냥 도와주고 싶었을 뿐이에요.
examples.en: I'm not anyone's savior, I just wanted to help.

examples.ko: 영화에서 구원자 역할은 늘 주인공이 맡아요.
examples.en: In movies, the role of the rescuer always goes to the main character.

explain: 위기나 어려움에서 건져 준 사람을 가리켜요. 종교에서는 사람을 구하는 존재를 말하기도 해요. 비슷한 말로 '구세주'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 친구가 제 구원자가 되어 줬어요.
phrases.en: That friend became my savior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-가 되다'를 붙이면 위기에서 도와준 역할을 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -가 되다 means someone took the role of rescuer.

phrases.example: 길을 잃었을 때 지도 앱이 구세주였어요.
phrases.en: When I was lost, the map app was a lifesaver.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구원자'와 비슷하고, 어려울 때 도움이 된 사람이나 물건에 가볍게도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 구원자; also used lightly for a person or thing that helped in a pinch.

phrases.en: He appeared like a savior and helped me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-처럼'을 붙이면 비유로 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -처럼 makes it a comparison.

explain_en: It refers to someone who pulls you out of a crisis or hardship. In religion it can also mean a being who saves people. A similar word is '구세주'.

t90.ax: That doctor is our family's savior.

examples.ko: 그 할머니는 말투와 몸짓이 귀부인 같아요.
examples.en: That grandmother's way of speaking and moving is like a noblewoman's.

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에 귀부인이 파티에 나오는 장면이 있어요.
examples.en: In the old movie there's a scene where a noblewoman appears at a party.
You came dressed elegantly, like a great lady.
It was a gathering of noble ladies, so I felt a little nervous.
I wore a noblewoman's dress and took photos.

examples.ko: 소설 속 귀부인은 늘 하얀 장갑을 끼고 다녀요.
examples.en: The noblewoman in the novel always wears white gloves.

explain: 신분이 높거나 부유한 집의 부인을 가리키는 말이에요. 요즘은 소설이나 영화 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 우아하고 품위 있는 모습을 비유할 때 '귀부인 같다'고도 말해요.

phrases.en: She walks elegantly like a lady.
phrases.nuance_ko: 품위 있는 모습을 칭찬하는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor praising someone's refined manner.

phrases.en: I took the role of a lady in the play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연극이나 영화에서 인물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about characters in plays or films.

phrases.example: 소설 속 귀족 부인은 항상 부채를 들고 있어요.
phrases.en: The noblewoman in the novel always holds a fan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀부인과 비슷하게 신분이 높은 부인을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 귀부인, refers to a woman of high status.

explain_en: It refers to a married woman of high status or from a wealthy family. Today it mostly shows up in novels and films, and people also say '귀부인 같다' to describe someone elegant and dignified.

t90.ax: I wore a noblewoman's dress and took photos.

examples.ko: 그분은 유명한 극작가라서 연극 대본을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: He is a famous playwright, so he has written many play scripts.

examples.ko: 극작가가 되고 싶어서 연극 동아리에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: I joined the drama club because I want to become a playwright.

examples.ko: 이 연극은 신인 극작가의 첫 작품이에요.
examples.en: This play is the first work of a new playwright.

examples.ko: 제 삼촌은 극작가로 일하면서 대학에서 가르쳐요.
examples.en: My uncle works as a playwright and also teaches at a university.

examples.ko: 극작가와 연출가가 만나서 대본을 같이 고쳤어요.
examples.en: The playwright and the director met and revised the script together.
Shakespeare is a playwright who represents England.

explain: 연극 무대에 올리는 글인 '희곡'을 쓰는 사람이라 '희곡 작가'라고도 해요. 영화나 드라마 대본을 쓰는 사람은 '시나리오 작가', '드라마 작가'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: He worked as a playwright for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극작가'와 같은 뜻이고, 쓰는 글인 '희곡'을 넣어 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '극작가', spelled out with '희곡' (the type of writing).

phrases.en: My dream is to become a playwright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장래 희망이나 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about future dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: Shakespeare is a world-famous playwright.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'을 앞에 붙여 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting '유명한' in front is a way to introduce a person.

explain_en: Since a playwright writes '희곡' (stage plays), people also say '희곡 작가'. Those who write scripts for films or TV dramas are called '시나리오 작가' or '드라마 작가'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 능글거리며 농담을 해요.
examples.en: He always cracks jokes with a smug, sly manner.
Stop being so slick and tell me honestly.
It was annoying to see him grinning slyly after doing wrong.
My boss acts so slyly that it's uncomfortable to deal with him.
My younger sibling slyly asked me for pocket money.
That friend is annoying every time he acts all slick.

explain: 속은 따로 있으면서 겉으로 뻔뻔하게 웃거나 말하는 행동을 가리켜요. '능글맞다'가 그런 성질을 말한다면, '능글거리다'는 그렇게 행동하는 모습에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그는 능글거리며 말해서 믿음이 안 가요.
phrases.en: He talks in a smarmy way, so I don't trust him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 말하는 태도를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -며 to link it with a way of speaking.

phrases.en: Don't be smarmy. Please speak seriously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뻔뻔한 태도를 그만하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to stop acting shamelessly.

phrases.en: I don't like his smarmy attitude.
phrases.nuance_ko: '태도', '웃음'과 같은 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for nouns like attitude or smile.

explain_en: It describes grinning or talking shamelessly while hiding what you really think. While '능글맞다' describes that quality, '능글거리다' focuses on the act of behaving that way.
